```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cuffari_2016_mesalamine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Cuffari_2016_mesalamine"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S95316>

Cuffari et al. ran a Phase I randomised open-label study (NCT01130844) of
once-daily multimatrix mesalamine (5-aminosalicylic acid, 5-ASA) at 30, 60 or
100 mg/kg/day (capped at 4800 mg/day) for 7 days in children and adolescents with
ulcerative colitis. Plasma and 0-24 h urine 5-ASA and N-acetyl-5-ASA (Ac-5-ASA)
were measured on day 7 and analysed by non-compartmental analysis (Table 2) and by
a joint parent-metabolite population PK model (Figure S1, Table S2). The model was
then used to simulate steady-state exposures by weight band for the Phase III dose
proposal (Figure 3, Tables S3 and S4).

# Population

Fifty-two subjects aged 5-17 years (mean 13.3 years; 25 children 5-12 years and
36 adolescents 13-17 years across arms) weighing 18-82 kg were randomised to 30
(n = 21), 60 (n = 22) or 100 (n = 9) mg/kg/day. Randomisation was stratified by
body weight (18-24, 25-49 and 50-82 kg); the lightest stratum received only 60 or
100 mg/kg/day and the heaviest only 30 or 60 mg/kg/day. 57.7% were female and
98.1% White (Table 1). Total daily doses ranged from 900 to 4800 mg, made up from
300, 600 and 1200 mg tablets.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Cuffari_2016_mesalamine")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. They are
collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: two parallel lagged first-order depots into a one-compartment 5-ASA central pool; renal (to urine) and metabolic (to Ac-5-ASA) clearance; one-compartment Ac-5-ASA with renal (to urine) and non-renal clearance | n/a | Results "Population pharmacokinetics"; Figure S1 |
| `lka` (Ka1) | 0.0334 1/h | Table S2 |
| `lka2` (Ka3) | 0.273 1/h | Table S2 |
| `ltlag` (ALAG1) | 5.10 h | Table S2 |
| `ldtlag2` (ALAG3, added to ALAG1) | 15.0 h | Table S2 and its abbreviation footnote; Results text |
| `logitfrel` (F1) | logit(0.734) | Table S2 |
| `lcl_renal` (CLR/F) | 1.15 L/h | Table S2; Results text |
| `lcl_met` (CLM/F) | 85.6 L/h | Table S2; Results text |
| `lvc` (Vc/F) | 109 L | Table S2; Results text |
| `lcl_renal_ac5asa` (CLRM/F) | 2.54 L/h | Table S2; Results text |
| `lcl_nonren_ac5asa` (CLNRM/F) | 74.4 L/h | Table S2; Results text |
| `lvc_ac5asa` (VcM/F) | 7.10 L | Table S2; Results text |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table S2 "~WT" rows; reference 70 kg from footnote a |
| IIV variances (11 etas) | 0.181, 0.115, 0.412, 0.133, 0.0823, 0.0225 FIX, 2.72, 1.87, 0.256, 0.0225 FIX, 0.662 | Table S2 omega^2 column |
| `propSd`, `propSd_ac5asa` | sqrt(0.136), sqrt(0.0829) | Table S2 sigma^2 (plasma) |
| `propSd_urine`, `propSd_urine_ac5asa` | 0.06 (fixed) | Table S2 sigma^2 = 0.0036 FIX (urine) |
| Ac-5-ASA formed per mg 5-ASA: 195.15 / 153.14 | 1.2743 | Molecular weights in Methods "Non-compartmental pharmacokinetic analysis"; see Assumptions |

# Virtual cohorts

Individual data are not public. Two virtual cohorts are built.

* **Study cohort** (Table 2 and Figure 2): 200 subjects per dose arm, with body
  weight drawn uniformly over the strata each arm was open to (30 mg/kg: 25-82 kg;
  60 mg/kg: 18-82 kg; 100 mg/kg: 18-49 kg). The daily dose is the mg/kg dose
  rounded to the nearest 300 mg tablet increment, at least 900 mg and at most
  4800 mg.
* **Dose-proposal cohort** (Tables S3 and S4): 200 subjects per weight band and
  dose level, weight uniform within the band (18-23, 24-35, 36-50 and 51-90 kg),
  with the paper's fixed low and high doses.

Both cohorts are dosed once daily for 7 days, as in the study, and summarised
over the day-7 dosing interval (144-168 h). Every dose is entered into both
depots; the model splits it with F1 and 1 - F1.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2016)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)

n_per_arm <- 200
n_days <- 7
dose_times <- (seq_len(n_days) - 1) * 24
day7_start <- (n_days - 1) * 24

# One subject per row: id, WT, daily dose, and grouping labels.
make_events <- function(subjects, obs_tad) {
  doses <- subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times, cmt = c("depot", "depot2")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = day7_start + obs_tad) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = NA_character_, amt = 0, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,       ~mgkg, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi,
  "30 mg/kg/day",      30,     25,     82,
  "60 mg/kg/day",      60,     18,     82,
  "100 mg/kg/day",    100,     18,     49
)
study_subjects <- arms |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), wt_lo, wt_hi),
    dose = pmin(4800, pmax(900, 300 * round(mgkg * WT / 300)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, WT, dose)

# 0.25 h grid over the day-7 interval for the profile figure; the paper's
# sampling times (0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 16, 24 h) are a subset of it.
study_events <- make_events(study_subjects, obs_tad = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25))

bands <- tibble::tribble(
  ~band,      ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~low, ~high,
  "18-23 kg",     18,     23,  900,  1800,
  "24-35 kg",     24,     35, 1200,  2400,
  "36-50 kg",     36,     50, 1800,  3600,
  "51-90 kg",     51,     90, 2400,  4800
)
proposal_subjects <- bands |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(low, high), names_to = "level", values_to = "dose") |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per_arm)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number() + 10000L,
    WT = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), wt_lo, wt_hi),
    level = factor(level, levels = c("low", "high"))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, band, level, WT, dose)
proposal_events <- make_events(proposal_subjects, obs_tad = seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(c(unique(study_subjects$id), unique(proposal_subjects$id)))
)
```

# Simulation

Concentrations are summarised without residual error (`Cc` and `Cc_ac5asa` are
the individual predictions), and the urine states are cumulative amounts in mg.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Cuffari_2016_mesalamine")

sim_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = study_events,
  keep = c("treatment", "WT", "dose"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tad = time - day7_start,
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = arms$treatment)
  )

sim_proposal <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = proposal_events,
  keep = c("band", "level", "WT", "dose"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - day7_start)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: day-7 plasma profiles by dose arm

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
sim_study |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_ac5asa), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    analyte = dplyr::recode(analyte, Cc = "(A) 5-ASA", Cc_ac5asa = "(B) Ac-5-ASA")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(conc), sd = stats::sd(conc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, mean, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0), ymax = mean + sd), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the day-7 dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Simulated mean (+/- SD) day-7 profiles",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 2 of Cuffari 2016."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The simulated profiles have the shape of Figure 2: nearly flat over the dosing
interval, a broad maximum around 6-9 h, a trough near 16 h, and a rise towards
24 h. The late rise is the depot-2 input, lagged by about 20 h after each dose,
and is the paper's "secondary peak at 24 hours post-dose". The 30 and 60
mg/kg/day levels (5-ASA about 1000 and 2000 ug/L) match Figure 2. The 100
mg/kg/day arm is higher than observed (about 3000 ug/L simulated against about
2000-2500 ug/L observed after the first hours); see the PKNCA section.

## Figure 3 and Tables S3 / S4: steady-state AUC by weight band

```{r tables-s3-s4}
auc_tau <- function(t, c) sum(diff(t) * (utils::head(c, -1) + utils::tail(c, -1)) / 2)

proposal_auc <- sim_proposal |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, band, level, dose) |>
  dplyr::arrange(tad, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_asa = auc_tau(tad, Cc),
    auc_ac = auc_tau(tad, Cc_ac5asa),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

proposal_summary <- proposal_auc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auc_asa, auc_ac), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "auc") |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, band, level, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_mean = mean(auc),
    sim_cv = 100 * stats::sd(auc) / mean(auc),
    sim_median = stats::median(auc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published_s3_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte,  ~band,      ~level, ~pub_mean, ~pub_cv, ~pub_median,
  "auc_asa", "18-23 kg", "low",     24100,    50.6,      22100,
  "auc_asa", "18-23 kg", "high",    47000,    50.0,      43100,
  "auc_asa", "24-35 kg", "low",     24600,    49.7,      22800,
  "auc_asa", "24-35 kg", "high",    49600,    50.0,      45700,
  "auc_asa", "36-50 kg", "low",     27000,    48.3,      25000,
  "auc_asa", "36-50 kg", "high",    54000,    49.1,      50000,
  "auc_asa", "51-90 kg", "low",     29700,    48.2,      27500,
  "auc_asa", "51-90 kg", "high",    59700,    47.5,      55500,
  "auc_ac",  "18-23 kg", "low",     33000,    42.1,      30800,
  "auc_ac",  "18-23 kg", "high",    66500,    42.7,      63100,
  "auc_ac",  "24-35 kg", "low",     34200,    43.9,      32400,
  "auc_ac",  "24-35 kg", "high",    68300,    44.6,      64700,
  "auc_ac",  "36-50 kg", "low",     37800,    42.5,      35700,
  "auc_ac",  "36-50 kg", "high",    75200,    42.3,      71600,
  "auc_ac",  "51-90 kg", "low",     41200,    41.8,      39200,
  "auc_ac",  "51-90 kg", "high",    82900,    41.4,      78900
)

s3_s4 <- proposal_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(level = as.character(level)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_s3_s4, by = c("analyte", "band", "level")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    analyte = dplyr::recode(analyte, auc_asa = "5-ASA (Table S3)", auc_ac = "Ac-5-ASA (Table S4)"),
    pct_diff_mean = 100 * (sim_mean - pub_mean) / pub_mean
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(analyte, band, level)

s3_s4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Analyte = analyte, `Weight band` = band, `Dose (mg)` = dose,
    `Mean, simulated` = signif(sim_mean, 3), `Mean, published` = pub_mean,
    `Mean diff (%)` = round(pct_diff_mean, 1),
    `CV% simulated` = round(sim_cv, 1), `CV% published` = pub_cv,
    `Median, simulated` = signif(sim_median, 3), `Median, published` = pub_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Day-7 AUC(0-24) (ng*h/mL): simulated vs. Cuffari 2016 Tables S3 and S4.")
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
proposal_auc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auc_asa, auc_ac), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "auc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    analyte = dplyr::recode(analyte, auc_asa = "5-ASA", auc_ac = "Ac-5-ASA"),
    level = dplyr::recode(level, low = "Low dose", high = "High dose")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(band, auc / 1000)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ level) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight band", y = "AUC(0-24) at day 7 (ug*h/mL)",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 3 of Cuffari 2016."
  )
```

```{r tables-s3-s4-check}
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed clearance, volume or molecular-weight factor moves every
  # band by 20% or more; the band-to-band spread is weight-distribution noise.
  abs(stats::median(s3_s4$pct_diff_mean)) < 10,
  stats::quantile(abs(s3_s4$pct_diff_mean), 0.9) < 20
)
```

The simulated means agree with Tables S3 and S4 to within about 15% in every
band (median difference `r round(stats::median(s3_s4$pct_diff_mean), 1)`%). The
largest shortfall is in the 51-90 kg band, where the simulated cohort is spread
uniformly over 51-90 kg; a cohort skewed towards the lighter end, as a pediatric
population would be, raises the AUC of a fixed dose. The ratio of Ac-5-ASA to
5-ASA AUC (about 1.4) matches the tables only with the molecular-weight conversion
in the formation term; without it the ratio would be about 1.1 (see
Assumptions).

The simulated CV is about 40% for 5-ASA and 35% for Ac-5-ASA against the
published 48-51% and 41-45%, and the simulated 2.5th-97.5th percentile range is
narrower than the published one (for example 22,100 (906-96,900) ng*h/mL for the
18-23 kg low dose). The published simulation design is not described beyond "80
subjects with 1,000 replications" in Trial Simulator, so the source of the extra
spread (uncertainty in the parameters, residual error, the number of doses before
steady state, or the eta scale of F1) cannot be identified; the centres agree.

# PKNCA validation against Table 2

NCA uses the paper's day-7 sampling times (0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 16 and 24 h after
the dose), with the interval 0-24 h after the day-7 dose.

```{r pknca}
sampling <- c(0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 16, 24)
nca_input <- sim_study |>
  dplyr::filter(tad %in% sampling) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, tad, Cc, Cc_ac5asa, dose)

run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc_df <- nca_input |>
    dplyr::transmute(id, treatment, time = tad, conc = .data[[conc_col]]) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))
  dose_df <- nca_input |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, dose) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
    dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      cmax = mean(cmax), auclast = mean(auclast), tmax = stats::median(tmax),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

nca_asa <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_ac <- run_nca("Cc_ac5asa")

published_asa <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~cmax, ~auclast, ~tmax,
  "30 mg/kg/day",   1884,    21411,  6.00,
  "60 mg/kg/day",   3825,    46173,  8.98,
  "100 mg/kg/day",  4314,    49213,  1.98
)
published_ac <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~cmax, ~auclast, ~tmax,
  "30 mg/kg/day",   2396,    30942,  9.00,
  "60 mg/kg/day",   4113,    58119,  7.48,
  "100 mg/kg/day",  4968,    63067,  1.98
)

nca_units <- c(cmax = "ug/L", auclast = "ug*h/L", tmax = "h")
cmp_asa <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_asa |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)),
  reference = published_asa,
  by = "treatment", units = nca_units, tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp_ac <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_ac |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)),
  reference = published_ac,
  by = "treatment", units = nca_units, tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_asa, caption = paste(
  "5-ASA day-7 NCA, simulated vs. Cuffari 2016 Table 2.",
  "Cmax and AUC are arithmetic means, tmax a median. * marks a difference above 20%."
))
knitr::kable(cmp_ac, caption = paste(
  "Ac-5-ASA day-7 NCA, simulated vs. Cuffari 2016 Table 2.",
  "Cmax and AUC are arithmetic means, tmax a median. * marks a difference above 20%."
))
```

```{r pknca-check}
auc_ratio <- c(
  nca_asa$auclast / published_asa$auclast[match(nca_asa$treatment, published_asa$treatment)],
  nca_ac$auclast / published_ac$auclast[match(nca_ac$treatment, published_ac$treatment)]
)
stopifnot(abs(stats::median(auc_ratio) - 1) < 0.2)
```

In the 30 and 60 mg/kg/day arms (43 of the 52 subjects) simulated mean Cmax and
AUC(0-24) agree with Table 2 within about 15% for both analytes, including the
dose-proportional step between the two arms. The 100 mg/kg/day arm is
over-predicted by 30-75%. The observed exposure in that arm (nine subjects) rose
less than proportionally from 60 mg/kg/day, which the paper notes and attributes
possibly to the 4800 mg cap and the lighter subjects in that arm; the published
model is linear in dose and scales clearance with weight, so it predicts close to
proportional exposure for a mg/kg dose, as the simulation shows. The
over-prediction is a property of the published model against its smallest arm,
not of the transcription, and the arm is too small to say more. Observed tmax is
spread over the whole interval (0-24 h in every arm) because the profiles are
flat, so the tmax medians are not informative.

# Urinary excretion against Table 2

```{r urine}
urine_day7 <- sim_study |>
  dplyr::filter(tad %in% c(0, 24)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, treatment, dose) |>
  dplyr::arrange(tad, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    xu_asa = diff(urine),
    xu_ac = diff(urine_ac5asa),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_absorbed = 100 * (xu_asa + 0.7847 * xu_ac) / dose)

urine_published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~pub_xu_asa, ~pub_xu_ac, ~pub_pct,
  "30 mg/kg/day",          162,        532,     29.4,
  "60 mg/kg/day",          298,        708,     27.0,
  "100 mg/kg/day",         235,        593,     22.1
)

urine_day7 |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_xu_asa = mean(xu_asa), sim_xu_ac = mean(xu_ac),
    sim_pct = mean(pct_absorbed), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(urine_published, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Arm = treatment,
    `Xu 5-ASA sim (mg)` = round(sim_xu_asa, 1), `Xu 5-ASA Table 2 (mg)` = pub_xu_asa,
    `Xu Ac-5-ASA sim (mg)` = round(sim_xu_ac, 1), `Xu Ac-5-ASA Table 2 (mg)` = pub_xu_ac,
    `% dose absorbed sim` = round(sim_pct, 1), `% dose absorbed Table 2` = pub_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Day-7 0-24 h urinary recovery: simulated vs. Cuffari 2016 Table 2.")
```

**The published renal clearances do not reproduce the observed urinary
recovery.** With CLR/F = 1.15 L/h against CLM/F = 85.6 L/h, the model sends about
1.3% of the systemic 5-ASA to urine, and with CLRM/F = 2.54 L/h against CLNRM/F =
74.4 L/h about 3.3% of Ac-5-ASA. The simulated 0-24 h urinary amounts are
therefore one-eighth to one-fifth of the Table 2 means, and the "% dose absorbed"
is about 5% rather than 22-29%. The non-compartmental renal clearances in Table 2
(5.0-6.5 L/h for 5-ASA and 10-16 L/h for Ac-5-ASA, as true rather than apparent
clearances) are also several-fold larger than the model's apparent values, which
should be the larger of the two. The plasma predictions, which depend only on the
sums CLR/F + CLM/F and CLRM/F + CLNRM/F, are unaffected. The renal clearances are
packaged exactly as printed in Table S2 and the Results text, which agree with
each other; the urine compartments should not be used for prediction until the
discrepancy is resolved.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Molecular-weight conversion in metabolite formation.** The paper does not say
  how the acetylation flux is converted. Ac-5-ASA is carried in mg of Ac-5-ASA,
  and each mg of 5-ASA cleared by CLM/F forms 195.15 / 153.14 = 1.274 mg of
  Ac-5-ASA (the molecular weights printed in Methods). This is the reading that
  reproduces the paper's own simulations: Tables S3 and S4 give an Ac-5-ASA to
  5-ASA AUC ratio of 1.37-1.39 in every band, which the model gives with the
  conversion (about 1.4) and not without it (about 1.1).
* **F1 and its random effect.** F1 is the fraction of each dose entering depot 1,
  and the remainder enters depot 2, so the total bioavailability is 1 and all
  clearances and volumes are apparent. The scale of the F1 random effect is not
  stated. An exponential effect with variance 0.662 would put F1 above 1, and the
  depot-2 fraction below 0, in about a third of subjects, so the effect is
  applied on the logit scale with the published variance. The printed 95% CI
  (0.413-1.06) is symmetric on the natural scale, which suggests F1 itself was the
  estimated quantity with a transformed random effect. Steady-state AUC does not
  depend on F1, so this choice affects only the shape of the profile.
* **Depot-2 lag.** ALAG3 is "the absorption lag time from depot 3 in addition to
  the lag time from depot 1", so the depot-2 lag is ALAG1 + ALAG3, each with its
  own random effect.
* **Allometric exponents.** Table S2 lists separate fixed exponents for each
  clearance (all 0.75) and each volume (both 1); they are carried as one shared
  exponent per parameter type, with the same values.
* **IIV variances.** Table S2's footnote gives CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1) for
  omega^2 above 0.15, but every printed CV equals sqrt(omega^2) x 100 (for
  example Ka1: sqrt(2.72) = 165%). The omega^2 column is used as the variance.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Weights are drawn uniformly over each arm's strata or each
  band, the daily dose is rounded to the nearest 300 mg tablet increment within
  900-4800 mg, and both cohorts are dosed for 7 days. The paper does not give the
  weight distribution of either cohort, the tablet combination per subject, or
  the number of doses in its steady-state simulation.
* **Urine.** The urine compartments and their residual errors are packaged as
  published, but they do not reproduce the observed urinary recovery (see
  "Urinary excretion against Table 2").
* No erratum or correction for this article was found (checked 2026-11-24).
